metadata.name: Neoconservatism (post-Cold War American school)
metadata.description: The American neoconservative synthesis associated with Irving Kristol and the post-Cold War primacy school: market institutions, public morality, limited social provision and active defence of democratic allies.
metadata.scope: American neoconservatism as synthesised by Irving Kristol (1983–2003), including post-Cold War American primacy and democracy promotion associated with PNAC. Domestic positions use Kristol’s explicit account rather than extrapolation from foreign policy alone. The school differs from libertarian minimal government and nationalist non-interventionism. Neither every member of an administration nor every later conservative is represented.
metadata.phrase: A society with market institutions and established civic values, protected by military strength and an active international role.
